confirmed: Criterion 3 holds for S1-O1. Every two weeks each student submitted a creative product (for example a composition or improvisation), and two external assessors independently scored all main-study submissions, blind to participant identity, group allocation, and timing of submission. The paper says it used performance-based rubric assessment instead of self-report instruments (PDF p. 7, Sections 3.5-3.6; p. 5, Section 3.2; p. 17, Section 7).

measure = expert_raters holds. The two assessors had 'expertise in music theory, composition, and creativity research' and took no part in instruction. Discrepancies greater than two points on any dimension were settled by discussion (PDF p. 7, Section 3.5).

construct = overall_creativity holds. The creativity rubric rates four dimensions on a seven-point scale (originality of musical ideas, overall musical value, inventiveness in development, expressive impact), and every analysis uses one 'creativity' score. An addition, not an error: the paper also does not say how the two raters' scores combine, and it gives no inter-rater reliability for the rubrics. The kappas of .78 to .86 are for the interaction-log codes (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 3.3; p. 7, Section 3.5; pp. 9-12, Tables 3-6).

No diversity outcome exists. The paper never compares different students' outputs for similarity, and homogenizing appears only as a risk in the literature review. So across_people does not apply, and diversity_detail correctly stays empty (PDF p. 4, Section 2.4).

ai_available_when_produced = yes holds. Table 1 ties ChatGPT-4 use to each rated product in the treatment arm ('Students used ChatGPT-4 for melodic and structural ideas, revising with AI feedback. Creativity was judged on originality'), and treatment students attached a screenshot or link of their ChatGPT interaction to each submission (PDF p. 6, Table 1; p. 5, Section 3.2; p. 7, Section 3.6).

question = with_ai and timing = immediate hold. All scored products come from the 12 biweekly measurement points during the intervention, no outcome was measured after AI was withdrawn, and the paper names withdrawal as future work ('whether these patterns persist once the AI is withdrawn'). No separate post-test is described, despite the 'pre-test–post-test design' label (PDF p. 5, Section 3.1; p. 8, top paragraph; p. 16, Section 5.3).

unit = participant holds for both contrasts. The MANCOVA has N = 36 and 38 (Table 6) and error df 69 (74 people minus group, three covariates, and intercept). The latent growth models estimate random intercept and slope variances across students (PDF p. 12, Tables 5-6; pp. 8-9, Results RQ1).

comparison_type = ai_vs_bau and direction = treatment_higher hold. The two learning environments were 'structured to differ only in the presence or absence of ChatGPT-4', with the same instructor. Adjusted creativity means are 4.71 vs 4.35, and creativity slopes are 0.315 vs 0.210 (PDF p. 5, Section 3.2; p. 6, text below Table 1; p. 12, Table 6; p. 9, Table 3).

Contrast 1 matches the PDF exactly. Table 5, Group, Creativity: df1 1, df2 69, F 7.216, p .009, η² .096. Table 6: 4.71 (Std. Error 0.18, N 36) vs 4.35 (0.17, 38). Table 4, Group: Pillai's Trace .047, df 2 and 68, F 3.982, p .023, η² .047. The RQ2 text repeats these values (PDF p. 9, Results RQ2; p. 11, Table 4; p. 12, Tables 5-6).

Contrast 2 matches the PDF exactly. Table 3 creativity intercepts are 3.281 (0.043) vs 3.004 (0.064) and slopes 0.315 (0.006) vs 0.210 (0.010), each with p printed '< .000'. The quoted slope sentence is on p. 8. Table 2 linear fit for creativity: CFI .961, TLI .953, RMSEA .021, SRMR .032. Fig. 1 is titled 'Latent growth trajectories by group (wk1–wk12)' with 'Estimated mean score' on the y-axis. No test of the group difference in intercept or slope is printed (PDF p. 6, Table 2; p. 8; p. 9, Table 3; p. 10, Fig. 1).

The Fig. 1 endpoints agree with Table 3 when time runs from 0 to 11: 3.281 + 11 × 0.315 = 6.75 and 3.004 + 11 × 0.210 = 5.31. These are the values that open question 2 reads from the figure (computed from PDF p. 9, Table 3; p. 10, Fig. 1).

For the audit, an inconsistency in the paper, not a coding error: in Table 4 the Group Pillai's Trace (.047) does not fit F(2, 68) = 3.982. With one hypothesis df and two outcomes, F = 3.982 implies a trace of about .105, and a trace of .047 implies F of about 1.68. The printed p (.023) fits the F. The Week 1 rows are off by about .01. The form records the printed values, as form-spec rule 8 asks (computed from PDF p. 11, Table 4).

Table 5 F and p values agree (F(1, 69) = 7.216 gives p = .009). The printed η² values sit about .001 above F/(F + 69), for example .0947 against .096 for Group on creativity. So the form's note that the paper does not say whether η² is partial is fair (computed from PDF p. 12, Table 5).

No outcome that bears on the three questions is missing. The analytical-thinking rubric scores accuracy, justification, depth, and transfer of reasoning, not creativity (p. 7, Section 3.3). The cross-lagged paths and end-point correlation relate the two constructs (p. 12, Table 7). The ENA and Markov results cover only the ChatGPT group's coded process moves (p. 14, Table 8; pp. 13-16, Figs. 3-6). The prior-ChatGPT-use row of Table 5 is a non-randomized covariate, not an arm contrast or unassisted work after AI use (pp. 5, 12-13).

The Week 1 conflict touches only the growth-model intercept, and the form already lists it in open_questions. The paper calls Week 1 scores baseline scores from tasks done 'prior to interventions', but Table 1 places ChatGPT-supported composition in Weeks 1-5 (PDF p. 5, Section 3.1; p. 6, Table 1; p. 9, Results RQ2).
summary: S1-O1 is a creativity score that two blinded external experts gave to the music products students submitted every two weeks, with ChatGPT-4 available to the treatment arm and never withdrawn, so scored_on_output, expert_raters, overall_creativity, participant, with_ai, and immediate all have explicit support in the PDF (pp. 5-7, 16-17). Every number in both contrasts matches Tables 2-6, Fig. 1, and the p. 8 text exactly, and no outcome that bears on the three questions is missing.
